messages:
Jon: Hey team — prototyping a 'rollout cost lens' in the console that combines token-level cost, per-model unit economics, and KV/cache savings per route. Big question: how should we attribute cache hits that are shared across routes (same cached prefix used by A and B)?
Maya: Love that. Product needs chargeback by feature so customers can see which routes are earning credits. UI idea: show both 'allocated credit' and 'shared credit' columns, default to conservative view. Toggle to switch model-vs-route breakdown.
Sam: Telemetry note: current logs include cache_hit events with prefix_id and request_route but we don't track stable "ownership" of a prefix. Two practical attribution heuristics: (1) first-writer gets full credit, (2) pro-rata split by downstream hits. Both feasible but different edge cases.
Priya: From analytics side, proportional split is doable offline. Quick SQL sketch: ```SQL
WITH hits AS (
  SELECT prefix_id, route, count(*) as hits, sum(tokens_saved) as saved
  FROM cache_events
  WHERE ts BETWEEN :start AND :end
  GROUP BY 1,2
)
SELECT h.prefix_id, h.route, h.hits, h.saved, h.hits / sum(h.hits) over (partition by h.prefix_id) as frac
FROM hits h;
``` Then join to rollout traffic slices to attribute to variants.
Ben: Practical ops concern — computing this at dashboard time is expensive. We should pre-aggregate hourly/daily and surface "estimated live" numbers with a confidence ribbon. Also watch out for cardinality explosion if we do full prefix x route joins.
Jon: UX compromise: default to first-writer attribution for realtime quick view, and provide an advanced "proportional attribution (backfill)" that runs as a background job and updates numbers later. Also show a small "confidence" badge.
Maya: @Sam @Priya can we get a projected-cost-delta column for canary rollouts? e.g., If we shift 10% -> 50% to variant B, show estimated token cost change and expected cache warmup effect. That would make rollback decisions clearer.
Sam: We can simulate traffic using sampled traces and our cost model (per-token unit price + model variant multiplier). Hard part is modeling cache warmup for new variants — need an estimated prefix overlap rate between variants.
Priya: I'll prototype a notebook to run Monte Carlo on sampled traces to estimate both immediate delta and 7-day steady state. We'll emit these as precomputed projection snapshots so the UI can be snappy. We'll include split of input_tokens vs generated_tokens too.
Ben: Also add throttling on the console side — if a user requests a full backfill attribution for a massive time range, queue the job and warn about cost. No ad-hoc heavy queries.
cost-bot: daily-rollup: canary-xyz projected delta = -3.2% (cache synergy), 95% CI [-4.5%, -1.1%] — dashboard: /dashboard/rollouts/xyz :chart_with_downwards_trend:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout "xyz" advanced to 20% @ 15:34 UTC :rocket:
Jon: OK action items — Priya to prototype monte-carlo projections, Sam to scope telemetry/backfill infra, Maya to draft UX copy and the confidence ribbon, Ben to add console request caps + user warning. I'll sync with everyone in tomorrow's 9:30 sync. Thanks! :thumbsup:
